heroHeadline: Carney Calls US Tariffs 'Relatively Modest,' Holds Off Further Retaliation as Trump Threatens Bombardier
heroSubtitle: Two days after Washington's Sept 8 bans on Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor vehicle imports, PM Carney signaled Sept 10 that Canada would not escalate further for now, calling the measures 'relatively modest' compared with earlier US actions and noting he remains in regular contact with Trump on other files. That restraint came despite a fresh flashpoint: Trump threatened Sept 7 to ban Bombardier aircraft sales in the US unless the Quebec planemaker builds domestically, a claim Bombardier disputed by pointing to its 3,500 US employees across 47 states. Finance Minister Champagne said Canadian and US officials remain in contact as Canada's TSX fell to an eight-day low Sept 9, while former ambassador Kirsten Hillman warned formal talks may not resume for months given Canada's firm red lines on steel and autos. In Mexico City, President Sheinbaum and Commerce Secretary Lutnick held a virtual USMCA call Sept 9 after weather grounded Lutnick's flight, with both sides calling the exchange 'cordial' ahead of the fourth bilateral review round.
